recipe.notes:
Frame: the model reads every input through its chat template - a system turn carrying the instruction, a user turn carrying the content, then the assistant header; the pooled token is the tokenizer post-processor's endoftext (id 151643) appended after it. The card frames a query exactly like a document: every usage example encodes queries without an instruction of their own, so the default "Represent the user's input." applies to both sides (format_model_input; the sentence-transformers prompts.default). The template therefore declares a query shape and a document shape with the same frame; the recipe's test renders the checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja at the pinned revision (hash-pinned) for one query and one document and requires both declared shapes to render the same strings. No template file ships (serve.chat_template null): every item rides the messages route as one conversation carrying its content only, and the engine frames it with the checkpoint's own chat_template.jinja - its default system message is the card's instruction, and with add_generation_prompt true (sent; vLLM's chat routes default it to false) it closes with the assistant header, so the engine's render is the declared frame, once; add_special_tokens true (sent) appends the endoftext anchor. The harness's template check reads that checkpoint file at the pinned revision and renders it over every conversation the client sends. A custom instruction is a different serving mode - a new template and judgement family, not this recipe (the pairs files carry no instruction field, and the reference refuses rows that carry one). The card's empty-input rule renders the text NULL, hence empty_doc: send_text "NULL": the client decides on the content before the frame, so an empty document ships NULL inside the user turn, as the card renders it. No query_max_tokens: the card caps the WHOLE prompt (MAX_LENGTH 8192) for both sides alike, mirrored by client.max_tokens.
Budgets: client.max_tokens is the declared policy, reserved frame-first with the content span cut (on_overflow: cut) and an item's media tokens reserved whole beside it; the embed client fits every request to it before shipping. The card's own truncation (the processor's truncation=True at max_length 8192) right-cuts the whole prompt: the frame's tail is cut and only the post-processor's endoftext is re-appended - the declared anchor_drop_over_cap deviation. reference.py renders exactly that cut (by character offsets on the rendered prompt, never a decode). The harness reports, in stage 1 and stage 2 alike, every text the client changed (its processing record: a budget cut counted with the frame) in the non-gating table under the declared deviation, and gates every other text exactly.
Media (the pixel pin). Serve: serve.mm_processor_kwargs pins {min_pixels: 4096, max_pixels: 1843200} under the nested images_kwargs scope - ONE shape across the media recipes, decided from the v0.31.0 tag source: the nested dict reaches the HF processor's images_kwargs (and through it the resize) and the vLLM-side image token budget, while the flat form also re-sizes every video clip (see sources). The checkpoint's own default is 4096..1310720 px (preprocessor_config.json), so the pin is load-bearing: unpinned, a page the client prepares above 1310720 px is resized again and counts other tokens. Capacity: one media item per request (serve.limit_mm_per_prompt image=1 video=1; client.max_images and max_videos carry the same numbers). Client half: image_processor qwen3_vl and client.image_policy with the same pixel numbers and engine_pixel_pinning true - the declaration that admits the card's 4096 px floor below the family's stock 65536 px - so the client resizes every image exactly as the card's fetch_image does (qwen-vl-utils smart_resize, factor 32) and counts it as the engine does. Media ride the messages route only, each item its own conversation, media before text (the card's format_model_input order). The harness's media stage holds the client's sent images (count, placement, prepared geometry, tokens) to reference.py --mode media and, against the engine, the engine's media count to the client's; the negative control that unpins the budget fails it (the pin's 1843200 px ceiling leaves the checkpoint's own 1310720).
Video, ONE declared sampling policy on every side (the reconciliation): a clip is sampled to 64 uniformly spaced frames over its whole length - client.video_policy {num_frames: 64, wire: video_url, engine_video_pinning: true}: the client sends the container as a video_url part (the multimodal embeddings lowering emits video_url per the policy) and the engine samples exactly those 64 frames, pinned with --media-io-kwargs '{"video": {"num_frames": 64}}' (serve.extra_args), which engine_video_pinning declares and the GPU wave must verify at /tokenize. It supersedes both older samplers: the served defaults of the checkpoint's video processor (fps 2, min_frames 4, max_frames 768) and the card script's container route (fps 1, max_frames 64). The reference side follows the same rule through the card's frame-list route (sample_frames at num_segments 64 keeps a 64-frame list unchanged). Not reconciled, and open for a video wave: the per-clip pixel budget - the engine and the client's container count use the checkpoint's video size (4096..25165824 px per clip), the card script caps a clip at total_pixels 7864320 (and 786432 px per frame); the media stage gates a container's token count against the engine (the engine's prompt-token difference to the same request without its media), and the generated media request set carries a 64-frame MJPEG AVI clip per size, alone and with text (observe.media_set, MEDIA_SET_VERSION >= 3), whose header the product's probe_video_header reads.

Per-size facts, read at the pinned revision. Architecture: Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration (config.json:architectures), model_type qwen3_vl; text_config.hidden_size 4096, 36 layers, 32 attention heads, 8 KV heads, head_dim 128, intermediate_size 12288, max_position_embeddings 262144, tie_word_embeddings false (config.json:tie_word_embeddings); vision_config.depth 27, hidden_size 1152, deepstack_visual_indexes [8, 16, 24], out_hidden_size 4096 (config.json:vision_config). Width: the served vector is 4096-d (1_Pooling/config.json:embedding_dimension); the card's Model Overview table says 4096 with an MRL range of 64..4096 (README.md). Weights: bfloat16 (config.json:dtype), 16,289,587,680 B = 15.17 GiB in 4 shards (model.safetensors.index.json:metadata.total_size); KV at the family's 8192-token serve.max_model_len is 2 x 36 layers x 8 KV heads x 128 head_dim x 2 B/token x 8192 = 1.21 GB = 1.1 GiB, so bf16 weights + KV fit one 80 GB-class GPU (resources.gpus 1, the family's). One forward of 8192 tokens stays inside the 32-bit envelope: attention q 32 x 128 x 8192 x 2 B = 6.7e7 B, MLP activations 12288 x 8192 = 1.0e8 elements; the served budget equals max_model_len (8192), so a full-budget prompt is a single chunk (no chunked-prefill path) and the pooling stall the larger pooling recipes meet at exactly max_model_len does not apply here. Family membership, every file byte- or JSON-identical to the 2b row at its own pinned revision: tokenizer.json (sha256 def76fb0..., the same 14 special added tokens including endoftext 151643, the same post-processor), chat_template.jinja (sha256 a47e6afb...), config_sentence_transformers.json (prompts.default "Represent the user's input.", similarity_fn_name cosine), sentence_bert_config.json (JSON-equal; the file differs only by a trailing newline), modules.json (JSON-equal; trailing newline), 1_Pooling/config.json (LAST pooling true, every other mode false; only embedding_dimension differs, 2048 -> 4096), preprocessor_config.json and video_preprocessor_config.json (JSON-equal: the image budget 4096..1310720 px and the served defaults fps 2 / min_frames 4 / max_frames 768 that the family's declared media policy pins and supersedes), and the vendored card script scripts/qwen3_vl_embedding.py (sha256 8ffa74a1...: MAX_LENGTH 8192, MIN_PIXELS 4096, MAX_PIXELS 1843200, FPS 1, MAX_FRAMES 64, MAX_TOTAL_PIXELS 7864320 -- every number the family's policy cites). The card's context is 32K (README.md) and the family's 8192-token serve.max_model_len is the reference's own MAX_LENGTH, unchanged for this size. The family's ONE reference loads this row's model and revision from --recipe (snapshot_download at the pinned revision); the media policy (nested images_kwargs 4096..1843200 px, one media item per request, 64 uniformly spaced video frames) is the family's declared one, copied here, not redesigned.
